subject: surgery
title: Testicular germ cell tumors, serum markers, radical inguinal orchiectomy, and retroperitoneal dissection

steps.tx: Testicular neoplasms represent the most frequent solid **malignancy** in young adult men aged fifteen to thirty-five years. Germ cell tumors comprise ninety-five percent of primary neoplasms, stratified clinically into seminomas and non-seminomatous germ cell tumors. Seminomas represent fifty percent of cases, composed of sheets of uniform cells with clear glycogen-rich cytoplasm, prominent nucleoli, and delicate fibrous septa infiltrated by lymphocytes. Cryptorchidism increases testicular malignancy risk four- to eightfold, even following successful early orchidopexy.
steps.say: Testicular tumors are the most common solid cancer in young men. Germ cell tumors are divided into seminomas and non-seminomatous subtypes. Cryptorchidism increases malignancy risk several fold, even after corrective surgical orchidopexy.

rows: Uniform clear cells with lymphoid stroma
Both AFP and beta-hCG may be elevated

steps.tx: Serum tumor markers play an indispensable **role** in the diagnosis, clinical staging, risk stratification, and post-treatment monitoring of testicular neoplasms. Alpha-fetoprotein has a serum half-life of five to seven days, produced by yolk sac elements and embryonal carcinomas, but never by pure seminomas. Beta-human chorionic gonadotropin has a half-life of twenty-four to thirty-six hours, produced by syncytiotrophoblastic cells. Serum lactate dehydrogenase reflects overall tumor cell turnover and metabolic bulk.
steps.say: Serum tumor markers include alpha-fetoprotein, beta-hCG, and lactate dehydrogenase. Alpha-fetoprotein is never produced by pure seminomas. Tracking marker half-lives verifies complete surgical resection and monitors treatment response.

steps.tx: A painless, firm intratesticular mass that does not **transilluminate** warrants immediate high-frequency Doppler ultrasonography. If an intratesticular vascular lesion is confirmed, radical inguinal orchiectomy with high ligation of the spermatic cord at the internal inguinal ring is mandatory. Transscrotal biopsy or scrotal orchiectomy is strictly contraindicated because violating the scrotal wall disrupts native retroperitoneal lymphatic drainage, predisposing to aberrant tumor dissemination into superficial inguinal lymph nodes.
steps.say: Any firm intratesticular mass requires prompt scrotal Doppler ultrasound. Radical inguinal orchiectomy with high cord ligation is mandatory. Scrotal incision or needle biopsy is strictly prohibited to avoid altering lymphatic drainage.

steps.tx: Staging requires abdominopelvic and chest computed **tomography** combined with serial post-orchiectomy serum marker decay kinetics. Primary lymphatic drainage from the right testis enters the interaortocaval and precaval nodes, while the left testis drains to the left para-aortic nodes. Seminomas demonstrate exquisite radiosensitivity and chemosensitivity to cisplatin-based regimens. Non-seminomatous tumors with persistent retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy exceeding one centimeter following induction chemotherapy mandate nerve-sparing retroperitoneal lymph node dissection to resect teratoma or viable residual carcinoma.
steps.say: Staging involves contrast CT imaging and post-orchiectomy marker monitoring. Seminomas respond exquisitely to radiotherapy and cisplatin chemotherapy. Persistent post-chemotherapy retroperitoneal masses in non-seminomatous disease require retroperitoneal lymph node dissection.
